parameters.definition_en: Hoek-Brown constant mb of the broken rock mass, used for the residual (post-peak) strength when residual is not set to peak. Cai et al. obtain it from a reduced residual GSI with σci and mi unchanged: mr = mi·exp((GSIr − 100)/28).
parameters.definition_es: Constante mb de Hoek-Brown del macizo rocoso roto, usada para la resistencia residual (postpico) cuando el residual no se iguala al pico. Cai et al. la obtienen de un GSI residual reducido, manteniendo σci y mi: mr = mi·exp((GSIr − 100)/28).
parameters.range_en: Below the peak mb: about 0.05·mi to 0.11·mi for residual GSI of 15 to 37 (0.96 to 2.14 with mi = 20)
parameters.range_es: Inferior al mb de pico: del orden de 0,05·mi a 0,11·mi para GSI residual de 15 a 37 (0,96 a 2,14 con mi = 20)
parameters.locator: Cai et al. 2007, section 1 (p. 248: residual parameters lower than peak), sections 3.2-3.3, eqs. 13 and 15 (pp. 253-255), Table 1 (p. 256: residual m = 0.964-2.138 for GSIr = 15.1-37.4, σc = 100 MPa, mi = 20); eq. 1 (p. 251: Ribacchi's alternative mr = 0.65 mb). The factor 0.05-0.11 is deduced: exp((GSIr − 100)/28) evaluated at GSIr = 15.1 and 37.4.

parameters.definition_en: Hoek-Brown constant s of the broken rock mass, used for the residual (post-peak) strength when residual is not set to peak; Cai et al. compute it as sr = exp((GSIr − 100)/9). For residual GSI below about 40 it is so small that it can be taken as zero.
parameters.definition_es: Constante s de Hoek-Brown del macizo rocoso roto, usada para la resistencia residual (postpico) cuando el residual no se iguala al pico; Cai et al. la calculan como sr = exp((GSIr − 100)/9). Para GSI residual inferior a 40 aproximadamente es tan pequeña que puede tomarse nula.
parameters.range_en: 0 to about 0.001 (residual GSI 15 to 37); always below the peak s
parameters.range_es: 0 a 0,001 aproximadamente (GSI residual 15 a 37); siempre inferior a la s de pico
parameters.locator: Cai et al. 2007, eq. 16 (p. 255), section 3.3.1 (p. 256: s negligible for GSI < 40) and Table 1 (p. 256: residual s = 0.000-0.001); eq. 1 (p. 251: Ribacchi's alternative sr = 0.04 s)

parameters.definition_en: GSI of the rock mass in its broken, residual state; the residual mb, s and a follow from it with the same equations as the peak values. Cai et al. obtain it by taking a residual block volume of about 10 cm³ and halving the large-scale waviness and small-scale smoothness ratings of the joints.
parameters.definition_es: GSI del macizo rocoso en su estado roto, residual; de él se obtienen mb, s y a residuales con las mismas ecuaciones que los valores de pico. Cai et al. lo calculan tomando un volumen de bloque residual de unos 10 cm³ y reduciendo a la mitad los factores de ondulación a gran escala y de rugosidad a pequeña escala de las juntas.
parameters.range_en: Below the peak GSI: GSIr/GSI = 0.37-0.51 for peak GSI 40-80 (residual GSI about 15-37 in the examples and case histories); for very weak rock masses GSIr ≈ GSI. Trend: GSIr ≈ GSI·exp(−0.0134·GSI)
parameters.range_es: Inferior al GSI de pico: GSIr/GSI = 0,37-0,51 para GSI de pico 40-80 (GSI residual de 15 a 37 aproximadamente en los ejemplos y casos reales); en macizos muy débiles GSIr ≈ GSI. Tendencia: GSIr ≈ GSI·exp(−0,0134·GSI)
parameters.locator: Cai et al. 2007, sections 3.2.1-3.3 (pp. 253-255: residual block volume 10 cm³; eqs. 9-11 residual joint condition; eq. 13 GSIr), Table 1 (p. 256), Tables 3-6 (pp. 257-261), eq. 18 and Fig. 18 (pp. 262-263: GSIr/GSI 0.37-0.51 for peak GSI 40-80); p. 251 (Russo's alternative GSIr = 0.36 GSI)

parameters.definition_en: mi used to compute the residual (post-peak) strength. Cai et al. keep it equal to the peak mi, because fracturing and shearing change the block size and joint condition but not the properties of the intact rock.
parameters.definition_es: mi con el que se calcula la resistencia residual (postpico). Cai et al. lo mantienen igual al mi de pico, porque la fracturación y el corte cambian el tamaño de bloque y el estado de las juntas, pero no las propiedades de la roca intacta.
parameters.range_en: Equal to the peak mi (about 4 for claystones to 32 for granite)
parameters.range_es: Igual al mi de pico (de unos 4 en argilitas a 32 en granito)
parameters.locator: Cai et al. 2007, section 3.3 (p. 255: σc and mi unchanged) and Conclusions (p. 263); range of mi: Hoek, Practical Rock Engineering ch. 11, Table 3, p. 6

parameters.definition_en: Disturbance factor D used to compute the residual (post-peak) strength parameters. Cai et al. use D = 0 for the residual state, because the rock mass is already damaged and the reduced residual GSI accounts for it.
parameters.definition_es: Factor de alteración D con el que se calculan los parámetros resistentes residuales (postpico). Cai et al. emplean D = 0 en el estado residual, porque el macizo ya está dañado y el GSI residual reducido lo tiene en cuenta.
parameters.range_en: 0 to 1 (definition of D); D = 0 recommended for residual parameters
parameters.range_es: 0 a 1 (definición de D); se recomienda D = 0 para los parámetros residuales
parameters.locator: Cai et al. 2007, section 3.3, text after eq. 17 (p. 255); bounds of D: Hoek et al. 2002, text after eq. 5

parameters.definition_en: Residual friction angle of the joint walls in Barton's criterion τ = σn·tan(φr + JRC·log10(JCS/σn)); it is the minimum shear strength of the joint. Barton and Choubey estimate it as φr = (φb − 20°) + 20·r/R, with φb the basic friction angle of dry sawn surfaces, r the Schmidt rebound on the wet joint walls and R on dry sawn surfaces.
parameters.definition_es: Ángulo de rozamiento residual de las paredes de la junta en el criterio de Barton τ = σn·tan(φr + JRC·log10(JCS/σn)); representa la resistencia al corte mínima de la junta. Barton y Choubey lo estiman como φr = (φb − 20°) + 20·r/R, con φb el ángulo de rozamiento básico de superficies serradas secas, r el rebote del esclerómetro Schmidt en las paredes húmedas de la junta y R en superficies serradas secas.
parameters.range_en: φr ≤ φb; φb of unweathered rocks 21-38° (most smooth unweathered surfaces 25-35°); 19-31° (mean 27.5°) in 136 tested joints; down to about 12° for weathered walls at low normal stress; 8-16° with softening clay coatings
parameters.range_es: φr ≤ φb; φb de rocas no meteorizadas 21-38° (la mayoría de superficies lisas no meteorizadas 25-35°); 19-31° (media 27,5°) en 136 juntas ensayadas; hasta unos 12° con paredes meteorizadas a baja tensión normal; 8-16° con recubrimientos arcillosos blandos
parameters.locator: Barton & Choubey 1977, eqs. 2 and 6 (pp. 4 and 15), eq. 7 (p. 15), Table 1 (p. 6: φb 21-38°), p. 4 (φb 25-35° for most smooth unweathered surfaces), p. 14 and Fig. 3 (φr as low as 12°, Richards 1975), p. 17 (φr 19-31°; conservative first estimate 20°), pp. 24 and 30 (mean 27.5°), p. 48 (Conclusions 1-2: minimum shear strength, independent of scale); Hoek 2023, ch. 4, eqs. 4-5 (PDF p. 82); Hoek 2023, Table 6, Ja column φr (PDF pp. 252-253, coated joints); FHWA 1989, p. 5.18

parameters.definition_en: Joint roughness coefficient: rates the roughness of the joint walls from 0 (smooth, planar) to 20 (very rough), by visual comparison with Barton and Choubey's ten standard 10 cm profiles or by back-analysis of tilt, push or shear tests. It decreases as the joint length grows (scale effect).
parameters.definition_es: Coeficiente de rugosidad de la junta: califica la rugosidad de las paredes de 0 (lisa y plana) a 20 (muy rugosa), por comparación visual con los diez perfiles tipo de 10 cm de Barton y Choubey o por retroanálisis de ensayos de inclinación, empuje o corte. Disminuye al aumentar la longitud de la junta (efecto escala).
parameters.range_en: 0-20 (standard profiles in steps of 2, from 0-2 smooth planar to 18-20 rough irregular); mean 8.9 in 136 laboratory joints
parameters.range_es: 0-20 (perfiles tipo en tramos de 2, desde 0-2 liso y plano hasta 18-20 rugoso irregular); media 8,9 en 136 juntas de laboratorio
parameters.locator: Barton & Choubey 1977, Fig. 1 (p. 5: JRC 20 rough undulating, 10 smooth undulating, 5 smooth nearly planar; completely smooth planar joints JRC = 0), eq. 3 (p. 7), Table 4 (p. 18), Fig. 8 (p. 19: profiles 0-2 ... 18-20), eqs. 11-12 (pp. 23-24: tilt test), p. 30 (mean 8.9), pp. 40-42 (scale effect: JRC 8.7 on 10 cm samples, 5.5 on a 45 cm joint); Hoek 2023, ch. 4, Figs. 5-6 and eq. 6 (PDF pp. 83-85, scale correction of Barton & Bandis 1982); FHWA 1989, Fig. 5.2 (p. 5.8)

parameters.definition_en: Joint wall compressive strength: the uniaxial compressive strength of the thin layer of rock at the joint walls. It equals the UCS of the intact rock for fresh (unweathered) joints and is lower for weathered walls; it is measured with the Schmidt hammer on the walls and decreases with joint size.
parameters.definition_es: Resistencia a compresión de las paredes de la junta: resistencia a compresión simple de la delgada capa de roca de las paredes. Es igual a la de la roca intacta en juntas sanas (no meteorizadas) y menor en paredes meteorizadas; se mide con el esclerómetro Schmidt sobre las paredes y disminuye con el tamaño de la junta.
parameters.range_en: From the UCS of the fresh rock (unweathered walls) down to about UCS/4 (conservative value for weathered walls when no Schmidt tests are available); 20-200 MPa (mean 92 MPa) in Barton and Choubey's tests; the Schmidt L-hammer covers about 20-300 MPa
parameters.range_es: Desde la resistencia a compresión simple de la roca sana (paredes no meteorizadas) hasta aproximadamente su cuarta parte (valor conservador para paredes meteorizadas sin ensayos con esclerómetro); 20-200 MPa (media 92 MPa) en los ensayos de Barton y Choubey; el esclerómetro tipo L cubre unos 20-300 MPa
parameters.locator: Barton & Choubey 1977, p. 4 (JCS 20-200 MPa in the tests), p. 6 and p. 8 (JCS = σc for unweathered joints; weathering stages 1-5), eq. 4 and p. 9 (Schmidt hammer, Miller 1965; 20 to at least 300 MPa), p. 7 and p. 12 (wet JCS 5-20 % lower), p. 12 and p. 17 (σc/JCS up to about 4; JCS = σc/4 conservative), p. 30 (mean 92 MPa), p. 42 (in situ reduction factors 2.5, 5 and 10), p. 47 (JCS rises to the confined strength when σn ≥ σc); Hoek 2023, ch. 4, eq. 7 (PDF p. 85) and upper limit σn = JCS (PDF p. 89); Hoek 2023, Fig. 1, UCS grades (R6 extremely strong > 250 MPa, PDF p. 93); FHWA 1989, pp. 5.7 and 5.18

parameters.definition_en: Dilation angle of the joint (program label 'Dilation Angle'): the angle between the shear movement and the joint plane, caused by the asperities riding over each other. Barton and Choubey found the peak value dn ≈ ½·JRC·log10(JCS/σn) as a lower bound (≈ JRC·log10(JCS/σn) when asperities suffer little damage), and zero for planar, clay-filled or previously sheared joints.
parameters.definition_es: Ángulo de dilatancia de la junta (etiqueta del programa 'Dilation Angle'): ángulo entre el movimiento de corte y el plano de la junta, debido a que las asperezas montan unas sobre otras. Barton y Choubey hallaron para el valor de pico dn ≈ ½·JRC·log10(JCS/σn) como límite inferior (≈ JRC·log10(JCS/σn) si las asperezas apenas se dañan), y nulo en juntas planas, rellenas de arcilla o ya cizalladas.
parameters.range_en: 0 (planar, filled or pre-sheared joints; also at the residual state) up to about JRC·log10(JCS/σn); mean peak values 6.8-26.5° by rock type in 136 laboratory joints
parameters.range_es: 0 (juntas planas, rellenas o ya cizalladas; también en estado residual) hasta aproximadamente JRC·log10(JCS/σn); valores medios de pico de 6,8 a 26,5° según el tipo de roca en 136 juntas de laboratorio
parameters.locator: Barton & Choubey 1977, eq. 8 (p. 21), pp. 30-31 (peak dilation angle; assumed zero for clay-filled, planar or pre-sheared joints; total friction ≥ φr + dn), Fig. 15 and eqs. 13-16 (pp. 32-34: dn between 0.5 and 2 times the asperity component), eqs. 20-21 and Tables 5-6 (pp. 35-36: means 6.8-26.5°, overall 20.0°); Cai et al. 2007, Fig. 3 (p. 250, after Barton et al.: roughness mobilized at peak and destroyed towards the residual state). Deduced: with the roughness destroyed (mobilized JRC → 0), eq. 13 gives a dilation that tends to 0 at the residual state.

parameters.definition_en: Shear strength of the joint after large displacement, once its roughness has been worn away. In Barton and Choubey's framework it is purely frictional, τr = σn·tan φr, with no cohesion and no roughness term.
parameters.definition_es: Resistencia al corte de la junta tras un desplazamiento grande, una vez desgastada su rugosidad. En el planteamiento de Barton y Choubey es puramente friccional, τr = σn·tan φr, sin cohesión ni término de rugosidad.
parameters.locator: Barton & Choubey 1977, p. 48 (Conclusion 1: φr is the minimum shear strength of a joint; planar or pre-sheared joints must be designed with it); Hoek 2023, ch. 4, eq. 2 and Fig. 1 (PDF pp. 78-79: residual cohesion drops to zero, slope φr). Deduced from the registry: the field has no unit (core/models.py, line 245), so it is not a stress in kPa; its role in the reference program is not documented in any source read.

parameters.definition_en: Coefficient of the power-law shear strength envelope τ = a·(σn + d)^b + c; it sets the level of the strength. With b = 1 the envelope is a straight line and a is the friction coefficient tan φ.
parameters.definition_es: Coeficiente de la envolvente potencial de resistencia al corte τ = a·(σn + d)^b + c; fija el nivel de la resistencia. Con b = 1 la envolvente es una recta y a es el coeficiente de rozamiento tan φ.
parameters.range_en: > 0 (deduced); with b = 1, a = tan φ (e.g. 0.7 ≈ tan 35°)
parameters.range_es: > 0 (deducido); con b = 1, a = tan φ (p. ej. 0,7 ≈ tan 35°)
parameters.locator: FHWA 1989, eq. 30 (p. 5.25) and Appendix 1, eqs. 30-31 (p. A1-3): Hoek and Brown's curved Mohr envelope τ = A·σc·(σn/σc − T)^B, the same law with a = A·σc^(1−B), b = B, d = −T·σc and c = 0; Table IV (p. 5.26: A = 0.042-1.220). Deduced from the form of the criterion: a > 0 so that strength grows with σn; a has units of stress^(1−b); with b = 1 and d = c = 0, τ = a·σn = σn·tan φ.

parameters.definition_en: Exponent of the power-law envelope τ = a·(σn + d)^b + c. b < 1 gives an envelope that flattens as σn grows (the instantaneous friction angle falls with stress), as observed for rough joints and jointed rock; b = 1 gives a straight line.
parameters.definition_es: Exponente de la envolvente potencial τ = a·(σn + d)^b + c. b < 1 da una envolvente que se aplana al crecer σn (el ángulo de rozamiento instantáneo disminuye con la tensión), como se observa en juntas rugosas y macizos fracturados; b = 1 da una recta.
parameters.range_en: 0 < b ≤ 1 for a concave or straight envelope (deduced); B = 0.53-0.71 in Hoek and Brown's envelopes for intact rock and rock masses
parameters.range_es: 0 < b ≤ 1 para una envolvente cóncava o recta (deducido); B = 0,53-0,71 en las envolventes de Hoek y Brown para roca intacta y macizos rocosos
parameters.locator: FHWA 1989, eq. 30 (p. 5.25) and Table IV (p. 5.26: B = 0.534-0.712); Barton & Choubey 1977, p. 3 (peak envelopes of non-planar joints are strongly curved; c and φ are stress-dependent). Deduced: the slope dτ/dσn = a·b·(σn + d)^(b−1) decreases with σn only if b < 1 and is constant if b = 1.

parameters.definition_en: Constant shear strength added to the power term of τ = a·(σn + d)^b + c: a cohesion-like offset that lifts the whole envelope. At σn = −d the power term vanishes and the strength equals c.
parameters.definition_es: Resistencia al corte constante que se suma al término potencial de τ = a·(σn + d)^b + c: un término de tipo cohesión que eleva toda la envolvente. Para σn = −d el término potencial se anula y la resistencia vale c.
parameters.locator: Deduced from the form of the criterion τ = a(σn + d)^b + c: for σn = −d the first term is zero, so τ = c, and c has stress units. The documented Hoek-Brown power envelope (FHWA 1989, eq. 30, p. 5.25) has no such term (c = 0).

parameters.definition_en: Shift of the normal stress in τ = a·(σn + d)^b + c: the envelope starts at σn = −d, so d is the tensile strength entered as a positive number. With d = 0 the material has no tensile strength.
parameters.definition_es: Desplazamiento de la tensión normal en τ = a·(σn + d)^b + c: la envolvente empieza en σn = −d, por lo que d es la resistencia a tracción, introducida como número positivo. Con d = 0 el material no tiene resistencia a tracción.
parameters.range_en: ≥ 0 (deduced); in Hoek and Brown's envelopes d = −T·σc with T from 0 to −0.14, i.e. 0 to 0.14·σc
parameters.range_es: ≥ 0 (deducido); en las envolventes de Hoek y Brown d = −T·σc con T de 0 a −0,14, es decir, de 0 a 0,14·σc
parameters.locator: FHWA 1989, eq. 30 and T = ½(m − √(m² + 4s)) (p. 5.25), Table IV (p. 5.26: T = −0.140 to 0). Deduced from the form of the criterion: (σn + d) = 0 at σn = −d, the most tensile normal stress the envelope reaches.

parameters.definition_en: Waviness angle i of the large-scale undulations of a joint (Patton's first-order projections): sliding has to climb the undulations, which adds i to the friction, τ = σn·tan(φ + i) for a cohesionless surface. A positive angle raises the strength; 0 means a planar surface.
parameters.definition_es: Ángulo de ondulación i de las ondulaciones a gran escala de la junta (proyecciones de primer orden de Patton): el deslizamiento tiene que remontarlas, lo que suma i al rozamiento, τ = σn·tan(φ + i) en una superficie sin cohesión. Un ángulo positivo aumenta la resistencia; 0 corresponde a una superficie plana.
parameters.range_en: ≥ 0 (0 = planar surface; deduced)
parameters.range_es: ≥ 0 (0 = superficie plana; deducido)
parameters.locator: Hoek 2023, ch. 4, eq. 3 and Fig. 4 (PDF pp. 81-82: Patton 1966, saw-tooth specimens; valid at low normal stress); FHWA 1989, p. 5.3 (Patton's equation for regular projections) and p. 5.4 (first-order projections = major undulations, which control field slopes; second-order = small steep bumps, sheared off as stress rises; Patton's sketch shows average first-order i of about 13-15°). Deduced: the lower bound 0 follows from the definition; how the angle combines with a power envelope (which has no single friction angle) is not stated in these sources.

parameters.definition_en: Coefficient a of the residual (large-displacement) power-law envelope τr = ar·(σn + dr)^br + cr, fitted to residual shear strengths in the same way as the peak a.
parameters.definition_es: Coeficiente a de la envolvente potencial residual (gran desplazamiento) τr = ar·(σn + dr)^br + cr, ajustado a las resistencias residuales igual que el a de pico.
parameters.range_en: > 0; it should give a residual envelope not above the peak one (deduced)
parameters.range_es: > 0; debe dar una envolvente residual no superior a la de pico (deducido)
parameters.locator: Hoek 2023, ch. 4, Fig. 1 and eqs. 1-2 (PDF pp. 78-79: peak and residual envelopes; residual strength remains constant at large displacement). Deduced: same form and bounds as a; residual strength is the minimum the joint keeps, so it cannot exceed the peak.

parameters.definition_en: Exponent b of the residual power-law envelope τr = ar·(σn + dr)^br + cr; same meaning as the peak b.
parameters.definition_es: Exponente b de la envolvente potencial residual τr = ar·(σn + dr)^br + cr; mismo significado que la b de pico.
parameters.range_en: 0 < b ≤ 1 for a concave or straight envelope (deduced)
parameters.range_es: 0 < b ≤ 1 para una envolvente cóncava o recta (deducido)
parameters.locator: Deduced from the form of the criterion, as for b.

parameters.definition_en: Constant shear strength c of the residual power-law envelope. The residual strength of rock discontinuities is usually taken as cohesionless, so this term is normally zero.
parameters.definition_es: Resistencia al corte constante c de la envolvente potencial residual. La resistencia residual de las discontinuidades suele considerarse sin cohesión, por lo que este término es normalmente nulo.
parameters.range_en: Normally 0
parameters.range_es: Normalmente 0
parameters.locator: Hoek 2023, ch. 4, eq. 2 (PDF p. 79: in the residual state the cohesion has dropped to zero); Cai et al. 2007, section 2.3 (p. 250: residual strength generally Mohr-Coulomb with near-zero cohesion). Deduced: c is the cohesion-like term of the residual envelope (see c).

parameters.definition_en: Normal-stress shift d (tensile strength) of the residual power-law envelope. A broken joint or rock mass keeps no tensile strength, so it is normally zero.
parameters.definition_es: Desplazamiento d de la tensión normal (resistencia a tracción) de la envolvente potencial residual. Una junta o un macizo roto no conserva resistencia a tracción, por lo que normalmente es nulo.
parameters.range_en: ≥ 0; normally 0
parameters.range_es: ≥ 0; normalmente 0
parameters.locator: Hoek 2023, ch. 4, eq. 2 (PDF p. 79: residual envelope τr = σn·tan φr through the origin). Deduced from the form of the criterion, as for d.

parameters.definition_en: Waviness angle of the large-scale joint undulations used in the residual envelope; same meaning as the peak waviness. Large displacements and higher normal stress can shear off the projections and reduce the effective angle.
parameters.definition_es: Ángulo de ondulación de las ondulaciones a gran escala de la junta usado en la envolvente residual; mismo significado que la ondulación de pico. Los grandes desplazamientos y las tensiones normales altas pueden cortar las proyecciones y reducir el ángulo efectivo.
parameters.range_en: ≥ 0 (deduced)
parameters.range_es: ≥ 0 (deducido)
parameters.locator: FHWA 1989, p. 5.4 (as normal stress increases the first-order projections are sheared off and the effective roughness angle falls towards zero); Cai et al. 2007, section 3.2.2 (p. 255: the large-scale waviness rating of the joints is halved for the residual state). Deduced: lower bound 0 from the definition.

parameters.definition_en: Ratio of the dilation angle to the friction angle mobilized on the Power Curve envelope at the current normal stress (the instantaneous, tangent friction angle): ψ = ratio·φi. 0 gives no dilation and 1 gives associated flow (ψ = φi).
parameters.definition_es: Razón entre el ángulo de dilatancia y el ángulo de rozamiento movilizado en la envolvente Power Curve a la tensión normal actual (ángulo de rozamiento instantáneo, tangente): ψ = razón·φi. 0 no da dilatancia y 1 da flujo asociado (ψ = φi).
parameters.range_en: 0 to 1 (deduced: 0 = no plastic volume change, 1 = associated flow; the dilation angle is generally smaller than the friction angle)
parameters.range_es: 0 a 1 (deducido: 0 = sin cambio de volumen plástico, 1 = flujo asociado; el ángulo de dilatancia es en general menor que el de rozamiento)
parameters.locator: Deduced from the definition of the quantity (ratio of two angles). Instantaneous friction angle: Hoek 2023, ch. 4, Fig. 7 and eqs. 8-10 (PDF p. 88). Dilation angle generally smaller than the friction angle, and associated flow overpredicting dilation: Davis & Selvadurai 2002, sec. 2.6 (p. 43) and sec. 4.5 (pp. 94-95).

parameters.definition_en: Tension cut-off T: the minor principal stress cannot exceed this tensile value (yield surface sigma3 - T = 0, associated flow). It truncates the apex of the shear envelope, which on its own would allow too large tensile stresses in a cohesive material.
parameters.definition_es: Corte a tracción T: la tensión principal menor no puede superar este valor de tracción (superficie sigma3 - T = 0, flujo asociado). Trunca el vértice de la envolvente de corte, que por sí sola admitiría tracciones excesivas en un material con cohesión.
parameters.range_en: 0 for a material without tensile strength (program default). Intact rock (77 Canadian rocks, CANMET Table 1): about 0.4-26 MPa.
parameters.range_es: 0 para un material sin resistencia a tracción (valor por defecto). Roca intacta (77 rocas canadienses, tabla 1 de CANMET): de unos 0,4 a 26 MPa.
parameters.locator: Vermeer & de Borst 1984 §6/7, pp. 43-44 (why the Coulomb apex is cut off); CANMET 1995 Table 1, column sigma_t (PDF pp. 102-109), min 0.43 MPa (coal) to 25.96 MPa (andesite), range computed from the table.
